knowledge.text: Limits of SMART-based prediction and vendor caveats / Many failures give no SMART warning: In the Google study, 56% of failed drives had no count in the four strongest SMART signals (scan errors, reallocation count, offline reallocation, probational count), and 36% failed with no SMART error at all apart from temperature ([3], as summarized in [1]). Backblaze reports that 23.3% of failed drives showed no warning in its five tracked attributes [2]. A low predicted risk is therefore not a guarantee of health.

Thermal attributes (SMART 190, 194) / How much temperature matters: The Google field study found little correlation between increased temperature and failure, and no correlation with usage level ([2], as summarized in [1]). In this system thermal evidence is weighted by the calibrated model rather than by fixed thresholds; a sustained rise relative to the drive's own baseline, or a short spike, is more informative than the absolute level.

Media health attributes (SMART 5, 184, 187, 197, 198) / Interpreting media signals together: Backblaze found that 76.7% of failed drives had at least one of SMART 5, 187, 188, 197 or 198 above zero, versus 4.2% of operational drives; so 23.3% of failed drives gave no warning in these attributes [2]. Growth within a short window is more informative than a static non-zero count [2].

Usage and wear attributes (SMART 9, 12, 193, 241, 242) / SMART 12: Power Cycle Count: The count of full power on/off cycles [1]. In a data center drives are rarely power-cycled, so jumps usually reflect maintenance events or chassis problems.
